label: Fall from height
summary: Falls from ladders, roofs, shelving, mezzanines and loading docks, and through skylights, fragile roof sheets, rotten floors and open shafts. A fall of 2 m can kill, and a broken leg far from help can be just as deadly.
signs: Fragile roofs: cement sheets, plastic roof lights and skylights
Open lift shafts, missing railings, hatches and pits
Wet, icy, mossy or dusty surfaces

Open manholes and missing storm grates: cast-iron covers get stolen for scrap, and flood pressure can push them off. Floodwater hides the hole, and people have died after falling into one, so don't walk or drive through flooded streets.
do: Stand a ladder on firm, level ground, about 1 out for every 4 up
Have someone foot the ladder, or tie it at the top
Keep three points of contact: two feet and a hand, or two hands and a foot
Let the ladder stick out about 1 m above the edge you step onto
Haul tools and parts up on a rope instead of carrying them
Stay off fragile roofs and skylights entirely
dont: Don't stand on the top three rungs of a leaning ladder, or the top two steps of a stepladder
Don't lean or reach out sideways from a ladder
Don't step on skylights, plastic roof lights or cement roof sheets
Don't work at height alone, in wind, or in the dark
Don't use shelving, chairs or boxes as ladders
Don't raise, carry or use a ladder, especially a metal one, within about 3 m of overhead power lines
ppe: Hard hat with the chin strap done up, so it stays on if you slip or fall
A harness only with an anchor good for about 22 kN (5,000 lb), a check before each use, and enough clear space below: OSHA’s worked example with a short lanyard needs 4.4 m (14.5 ft)
Retire a harness that has caught a fall, or whose history you don’t know
Never work at height alone: hanging in a harness can kill in under 30 minutes
firstAid: Don't move someone who fell from height unless they are in danger where they lie, or they are unconscious and might choke: then roll them onto their side, keeping head, neck and body in line
Keep the head and neck still if they have neck or back pain, numbness or weakness, or are unconscious or confused
Check breathing; start CPR if they aren't breathing normally
Splint suspected broken bones and get medical help
A head injury with confusion, vomiting or drowsiness needs urgent medical care
